source.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays

accepted.question_text: For the Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_θu)(t) with smooth data and a uniform mesh I_h, let u_h \in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) be the collocation solution and let u_h^{it} be the associated iterated collocation solution. Does the optimal local error estimate proved in Theorem 2.2 still hold for this more general equation when b(t) is not identically zero?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.2 Assume that the given functions g, K0 and K1 in the VFIE (1.3) are arbitrarily smooth, with b(t) \equiv 0, and let uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) be the collocation solution to (1.3) corresponding to the m Gauss points {ci} in (2.2), with uniform mesh Ih.

Open Problem 2.1 Let uit h be the iterated collocation corresponding to the collocation solution uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) (defined in (2.12)), and assume that Ih is a uniform mesh. Does the optimal error estimate of Theorem 2.2 remain true for the more general VFIE (1.3) with (smooth) b(t) \equiv 0?

accepted.question_text: How do the best local superconvergence constants C_m(q) in Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 depend on the proportional-delay parameter q, especially in the limiting regime q 	o 1^-?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.2 Analyse the dependence of the (‘best’) error constants Cm(q) in the optimal local superconvergence estimates of Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 on q, especially as q 	o 1−.

accepted.question_text: Suppose the Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_θu)(t) is solved on a uniform mesh by collocation in the continuous piecewise-polynomial space S^{(0)}_m(I_h), with collocation points X_h as in (2.2) and initial value u_h(0) = g(0)/(1 - b(0)) under the assumption |b(t)| < 1 on I. Does the associated iterated collocation solution retain the optimal local superconvergence orders from Theorem 2.2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3 Suppose that the VFIE (1.3) is solved by collocation in the continuous piecewise polynomial space S(0) m (Ih), with uniform mesh Ih, collocation points Xh given in (2.2), and initial value uh(0) = g(0)/(1−b(0)) (assuming |b(t)| < 1 on I). Do the optimal local superconvergence orders of Theorem 2.2 remain valid for the iterated collocation associated with this uh?

accepted.question_text: For the multi-delay pantograph-type Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = g(t) + \sum_{j=1}^r b_j(t)u(θ_j(t)) + \sum_{j=1}^r (V_{θ_j}u)(t) on a uniform mesh, where θ_j(t) = q_j t and 0 < q_1 < \cdots < q_r < 1 with r \ge 2, what are the optimal global and local convergence orders of the collocation solution and of the iterated collocation solution?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.4 Establish the optimal (global and local) orders of convergence of the collocation and iterated collocation solutions (on uniform meshes) for the multi-delay pantograph-type VFIE u(t) = g(t) +∑r j=1 bj (t)u(θj (t) +∑r j=1 (Vθj u)(t), t \in I

accepted.question_text: Consider the neutral Volterra functional integro-differential equation u'(t) = a(t)u(t) + b(t)u(θ(t)) + c(t)u'(θ(t)) + \int_0^t [K_{0,0}(t,s)u(s) + K_{0,1}(t,s)u'(s)]ds + \int_0^{θ(t)} [K_{1,0}(t,s)u(s) + K_{1,1}(t,s)u'(s)]ds on a uniform mesh, with θ(t) = qt and 0 < q < 1. If u_h \in S^{(0)}_m(I_h) is the collocation solution at Gauss points, is the optimal pointwise superconvergence order p* equal to 2m for m = 1,2 and m + 2 for m > 2, and can one also choose collocation parameters so that the same estimate holds for u'_h?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 Suppose that uh \in S(0) m (Ih) is the collocation solution to the initial-value problem for the neutral VFIDE (3.1) with respect to the Gauss points {ci} in (2.2) with θ(t) = qt (0 <q< 1). Prove that for sufficiently smooth data, the optimal order of superconvergence of uh at the points of a uniform mesh Ih, max t\inIh |u(t) − uh(t)| \le Cm(q)hp* , is given by p* = { 2m, m = 1, 2, m + 2, m> 2. Are there collocation parameters {ci} so that the above estimate is also true for u' h?

accepted.question_text: For the weakly singular Volterra functional integro-differential equation u'(t) = a(t)u(t) + b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_αu)(t) + (V_{θ,α}u)(t), where (V_αu)(t) = \int_0^t (t-s)^{-α}K_0(t,s)u(s)\,ds and (V_{θ,α}u)(t) = \int_0^{θ(t)} (t-s)^{-α}K_1(t,s)u(s)\,ds with 0 < α < 1, does collocation by u_h \in S^{(0)}_m(I_h) attain the global order \|u-u_h\|_\infty \le C_m(r)N^{-(m+1-α)} on graded meshes t_n = (n/N)^r T when the collocation parameters satisfy \int_0^1 \prod_{i=1}^m (s-c_i)\,ds = 0 and r \ge (m+1-α)/(2-α)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 Assume that the given functions a, b, g, K0, K1 in the weakly singular VFIDE (3.3) have continuous derivatives of order m + 1, and let uh \in S(0) m (Ih) be the collocation solution to (3.3). If the collocation parameters {ci} in (2.2) satisfy ∫ 1 0 ∏m i=1 (s − ci)ds = 0 and if the mesh is chosen to be Ih = {tn := (n/N) rT (0 \le n \le N)}, with r = r(α) \ge (m + 1 − α)/(2 − α), then, for θ \in C^{m+1}(I) satisfying (N1) and (N2) and for all 0 <α< 1, \|u − uh\|∞ \le Cm(r)N −(m+1−α).

accepted.question_text: For the weakly singular Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_αu)(t) + (V_{θ,α}u)(t) with 0 < α < 1, if u_h \in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) is the collocation solution and u_h^{it} is the associated iterated collocation solution, does one have the graded-mesh estimate \|u-u_h^{it}\|_\infty \le C_m(r)N^{-(m+1-α)} on meshes t_n=(n/N)^rT whenever r \ge m/(1-α)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2 Let the given functions g, K0, K1 in the VFIE (3.4) have continuous derivatives of order m+ 1, let b(t) \equiv 0, and assume that the delay function θ is subject to conditions (N1)–(N3) with d = m + 1 in (N3). If uit h is the iterated collocation solution corresponding to the collocation solution uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) for (3.4), and if the collocation points are as in Conjecture 3.1, then for graded meshes of the form Ih := {tn = (n/N) rT (0 \le n \le N)}, with r = r(α) \ge m/(1 − α), we have \|u − uit h \|∞ \le Cm(r)N −(m+1−α).

accepted.question_text: For the weakly singular Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_αu)(t) + (V_{θ,α}u)(t), analyze whether the analogue of Theorem 2.2 continues to hold on graded meshes of the form t_n = (n/N)^r T with r \ge m/(1-α).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.2 In analogy to Open Problem 2.1, analyse the extension of Theorem 2.2 to the weakly singular VFIE (3.4) with b(t) \equiv 0, for graded meshes of the form (3.7).

accepted.question_text: If the delay function θ satisfies the vanishing-delay conditions θ(0)=0, θ(t) \le q_1 t on I for some q_1 \in (0,1), and θ \in C^d(I), but θ is not strictly increasing on I, what convergence theory holds for piecewise-polynomial collocation solutions of the Volterra functional integro-differential and integral equations considered in the paper?

evidence.quote: The convergence analysis of piecewise polynomial collocation solutions to VFIDEs (1.2) and VFIEs (1.3) with vanishing delay functions θ that satisfy (N2) and (N3) but are not strictly increasing on I remains open but is currently being studied

accepted.question_text: Consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = g(t) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds for t \ge 0, where g is continuous and bounded on \mathbb{R}_+. For which continuous or weakly singular convolution kernels k_0 and k_1 do all solutions satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t) = 0?

evidence.quote: The analysis of the asymptotic stability of numerical schemes—in particular Runge-Kutta and collocation methods—for solving VFIEs with vanishing delays ought to be based on the linear test VFIE u(t) = g(t) + ∫ t 0 k0(t − s)u(s)ds + ∫ qt 0 k1(t − s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0. (4.6)

Open Problem 4.1 (a) (i) Let g be a continuous and bounded function on R+. Which (continuous, or weakly singular) convolution kernels, k0 and k1, does the solution of the linear test FVIE (4.6) satisfy (4.2)?

accepted.question_text: Given a continuous bounded function g on \mathbb{R}_+, do there exist continuous functions b, k_0, and k_1 such that every solution of u(t) = g(t) + b(t)u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds is asymptotically stable, meaning \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t)=0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 (a) (ii) If g is as in (1), are there continuous functions b, k0 and k1 so that the solutions of u(t) = g(t)+b(t)u(qt)+∫ t 0 k0(t−s)u(s)ds ∫ qt 0 k1(t−s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0, (4.7) satisfy (4.2)?

accepted.question_text: Assume the test Volterra functional integral equations (4.6) and (4.7) are asymptotically stable. If they are approximated on a uniform mesh by collocation in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) together with the corresponding iterated collocation solution u_h^{it}, for which collocation parameters {c_i} do both u_h(t) and u_h^{it}(t) converge to 0 as t 	o \infty?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 (b) Assume that the solutions of the test VFIEs, (4.6) and (4.7), are asymptotically stable. If they are approximated by collocation in S(−1) m−1(Ih), with uniform mesh Ih, and by the corresponding iterated collocation solution uit h, for which collocation parameters {ci} do lim t	o\infty uh(t)=0, lim t	o\infty uit h(t)=0 hold?

accepted.question_text: Consider the linear Volterra functional integro-differential equation u'(t) = a u(t) + b u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds for t \ge 0, where the corresponding pantograph equation without the integral terms is already asymptotically stable. For which continuous or weakly singular kernels k_0 and k_1 do the nontrivial solutions of this test equation still satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t)=0?

evidence.quote: For VFIDEs with vanishing delays we consider the linear test equation u'(t) = au(t) + bu(qt) + ∫ t 0 k0(t − s)u(s)ds + ∫ qt 0 k1(t − s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0. (4.8)

Open Problem 4.2 (a) Assume that the coefficients a and b in the pantograph equation (4.1) (or (4.4)) are such that its solution is asymptotically stable (i.e., assume (4.3) or (4.5)). Which (continuous, or weakly singular) convolution kernels k0 and k1 do nontrivial solutions of the linear test VFIDE (4.8) satisfy (4.2)?

accepted.question_text: Let the test Volterra functional integro-differential equation (4.8) have asymptotically stable exact solutions. If it is solved on a uniform mesh by collocation in S^{(0)}_m(I_h), for which collocation parameters {c_i} does the collocation solution u_h(t) also satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u_h(t)=0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 (b) Let (4.8) be such that its solutions u are asymptotically stable. If this test VFIDE is solved by collocation in S(0) m (Ih), with uniform mesh Ih, for which collocation parameters {ci} does lim t	o\infty uh(t)=0 hold?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the answers to the asymptotic-stability questions for the proportional-delay case θ(t)=qt, 0<q<1, are known. Do those answers remain valid when the delay is replaced by a nonlinear function θ satisfying the paper's conditions (N1)–(N3)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 Suppose that answers to Open Problems 4.1 and 4.2 are known (for the delay function θ(t) = qt, 0 <q< 1). Do they remain valid for nonlinear θ satisfying conditions (N1)–(N3)?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record through DOI 10.1007/s11464-009-0001-0 to the Springer PDF and mapped Sections 2-4 as the main open-problem regions on PDF pages 8-17.
Extracted numbered open problems 2.1-2.4 from the collocation and superconvergence discussion.
Extracted Open Problem 3.1, Conjectures 3.1-3.2, Open Problem 3.2, and the explicit statement that the non-monotone-delay convergence analysis remains open.
Extracted Open Problems 4.1(a)(i)-(ii), 4.1(b), 4.2(a)-(b), and 4.3 from the asymptotic-stability section.
Rewrote each item into a standalone question by inlining the relevant equation family, mesh assumptions, and asymptotic-stability or superconvergence target from nearby source text.

Kept the numbered open problems and conjectures as separate canonical items; the concluding remarks were treated as duplicates or summaries except for the non-monotone-delay statement, which was preserved as its own open question.
All accepted items have page-grounded verbatim evidence from the PDF, avoid dangling references, and introduce no facts beyond the cited equations and statements.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/current-work-and-open-problems-in-the-numerical-analysis-of-volterra-functional-equations-with-vanishing-delays.json and outputs/latest.json.
